title: Vinyl Plank vs Engineered Hardwood for Resale in Lynnwood
meta: Vinyl plank or engineered hardwood for resale in Lynnwood? LVP wins under about $850K and in townhomes; engineered wood earns its premium above that. Wills Flooring explains.
keywords: vinyl plank vs engineered hardwood resale, LVP or hardwood for resale value, best flooring to sell a house Lynnwood, vinyl plank resale value, engineered hardwood resale value, flooring before selling Lynnwood WA

blocks.lead: For most Lynnwood homes selling under roughly $850,000, and for nearly all townhomes, a quality rigid-core vinyl plank returns as much at sale as engineered hardwood at a lower cost. Above that price, or in a home where the neighbors have real wood, engineered hardwood earns its premium back.
blocks.detail: Lynnwood buyers are practical: many are first-time buyers or families moving up from a condo, and they care that the floor is new, continuous and hard-surface far more than what it is made of. The exception is the move-up buyer comparing your Meadowdale house to one with oak.

blocks.html: A common Reddit thread asks whether putting vinyl plank in a house before listing is "cheaping out" in the eyes of buyers. In Lynnwood the honest answer depends on the house. A 1970s Alderwood split-level with dated carpet and a $780,000 list price does not lose a single showing to LVP. A 2,400 sq ft Meadowdale home listed at $1.1 million competing with remodeled neighbors that have white oak might. Below is how we walk sellers through the decision at the showroom on 196th, with real labor numbers.

blocks.text: First, check what is already under the carpet

blocks.title: The Lynnwood shortcut:
blocks.text: A large share of 1960s to 1980s ramblers and split-levels in Alderwood, Martha Lake and Meadowdale have original oak under the carpet. If yours does, refinishing it at $3.99 per sq ft beats both new options for resale, because buyers pay for "original hardwood floors" in the listing. Pull a corner of carpet in a closet before you price anything new.
How Lynnwood buyers actually read each floor

items.title: The first-time buyer
items.text: Coming from a rental or a condo near the light rail, this buyer wants move-in ready and low maintenance. Wide, matte, wood-look vinyl plank photographs as new and reads as an upgrade over any carpet. They will not ask what it is made of, but they will notice cheap, glossy, repeating-pattern plank.

items.title: The move-up family
items.text: Selling a townhome to buy a 4-bedroom near Meadowdale or Lynnwood High. This buyer has toured homes with real wood and notices the difference underfoot and in sound. Engineered hardwood in the living areas is a tiebreaker against a comparable house with LVP.

items.title: The investor
items.text: Buying to rent near the Lynnwood City Center station. Vinyl plank is a plus for them: waterproof, tenant-proof, replaceable per plank. Hardwood is a liability they will have to protect. If your street is turning into rentals, LVP is the safer bet.

items.title: The appraiser and the agent
items.text: Listing agents in Snohomish County describe LVP as "luxury vinyl plank flooring" and hardwood as "hardwood floors" in remarks. Appraisers give credit for new hard-surface flooring either way, and rarely adjust much between the two under about $900,000.

blocks.text: Which one, by Lynnwood home type

a.title: Choose LVP when
items: The home is a townhome or condo near the City Center or Alderwood
List price is under about $850,000 and comps have carpet or LVP
You want one floor through the kitchen, baths and laundry
The lower level of the split sits on a slab
The likely buyer is an investor or a first-time buyer

b.title: Choose engineered when
items: Comparable listings in Meadowdale or Martha Lake show real wood
List price is above about $1 million
The main floor is one large open living area buyers will judge underfoot
You may stay a few more years and want a floor that can be refinished
There is no original oak under the carpet to bring back

blocks.text: Mistakes that lose money with either floor

items.html: Buying the cheapest plank. Thin, glossy vinyl with a 6 mil wear layer and an obvious repeat pattern reads as "flipper floor" to Lynnwood buyers and their agents. If you go LVP, go 20 mil, matte, with a long plank and embossed texture.

Mixing three floors on one level. Plank in the living room, old tile in the kitchen, carpet in the hall. Continuous flooring adds more perceived value than the material itself. See how we handle transitions in Lynnwood homes if you must mix.
Covering original oak. Laying anything over a sound 1970s oak floor throws away the cheapest upgrade available to you.
Chasing a trend color. Very gray plank is already dating. Warm mid-tone browns and natural oak looks sell to the widest pool of buyers in 2027.
Skipping subfloor prep to save a day. Rigid plank telegraphs every hump in a 1960s subfloor. Buyers feel the ridges even when they cannot see them.
Installing during the last week before photos. Both floors need a few days for baseboards, caulk and cleanup. Schedule three weeks ahead of the listing date.

blocks.text: What to settle before you order anything

items: Pull a carpet corner in two rooms and see whether oak is hiding underneath.
Ask your agent for the three closest comps and what flooring they show in photos.
Decide whether the kitchen and baths will get the same floor; that decision alone often picks LVP.
Measure every room and staircase, or let us measure at the free estimate.
Pick a plank or wood from samples in your own light, not under showroom bulbs. Our mobile showroom brings both to your Lynnwood home.
Get the labor, material, removal and prep in one written quote so you can compare the total, not the per-foot rate.

faq.q: Does vinyl plank hurt resale value in Lynnwood?
faq.a: Not in most price bands. Under roughly $850,000, and in townhomes and condos, quality rigid-core LVP returns as much as engineered hardwood because buyers value new, continuous, hard-surface flooring over the material itself. It only hurts when cheap plank is used, or when the competing listings all have real wood.

faq.q: How much more does engineered hardwood cost to install than vinyl plank?
faq.a: At Wills Flooring's published rates, installation labor is $3.25 per sq ft for engineered hardwood versus $2.50 for vinyl plank, and $125 versus $100 per stair. On a 1,100 sq ft level the labor gap is about $825. Material adds to the difference, since engineered wood generally costs more per foot than plank.

faq.q: Should I refinish the old oak or replace it with vinyl plank before selling?
faq.a: Refinish it. Original hardwood in a 1960s or 1970s Lynnwood rambler is a selling point that costs $3.99 per sq ft to bring back, less than installing new plank once you count material and carpet removal. Only replace it if the boards are water-damaged, sanded too thin or badly patched.

faq.q: What flooring do Lynnwood townhome buyers prefer?
faq.a: Vinyl plank, in practice. Townhome buyers are usually first-time buyers who want low maintenance and a floor that runs through the kitchen and half bath without transitions. A quiet underlayment matters more than the material, since shared walls and stacked floors make hollow sound noticeable.

faq.q: Is engineered hardwood worth it in a Meadowdale or Martha Lake home over $1 million?
faq.a: Usually yes. At that price your buyer is comparing you against remodeled homes with white oak or similar, and a vinyl floor becomes a reason to negotiate. Engineered hardwood in the main living areas, with LVP or tile in wet rooms, is the combination that photographs and shows best in that bracket.

faq.q: Which vinyl plank looks most like hardwood to buyers?
faq.a: A matte finish, planks at least 7 inches wide and 48 inches long, a 20 mil wear layer, embossed-in-register texture that follows the printed grain, and at least 20 unique plank faces so the pattern does not repeat visibly. Avoid high gloss and very gray tones. We bring these to your house so you can compare them in your own light.
